paper.title: Towards Scalable and Robust Structured Bandits: A Meta-Learning Framework

settings.name_in_paper: General structured bandit with feature-based hierarchical model (Bayes regret)
unmapped: parameter factorizes over N items, theta_i ~ g(theta_i | x_i, gamma) with item features x_i and meta-parameter gamma ~ Q(gamma)
observations Y_t ~ f(Y_t|A_t, theta) with reward R_t = f_r(Y_t; eta) for known eta
settings.definition_quote: \vgamma \sim Q(\vgamma), \theta_i| \vx_i, \vgamma \sim g(\theta_i|\vx_i, \vgamma), \forall i \in [N], \boldsymbol{Y}_t \sim f(\boldsymbol{Y}_t|A_t, \vthe), R_t = f_r(\boldsymbol{Y}_t ; \veta)

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial semi-bandits with linear mixed model (Gaussian)
unmapped: item means theta_i ~ N(x_i^T gamma, sigma_1^2) with known sigma_1 and item features x_i in R^d; gamma ~ N(mu_gamma, Sigma_gamma) with known prior
feasible actions are subsets of [N] of size at most K satisfying application-specific constraints
settings.definition_quote:
heta_i \sim 
ormal(\vx_i^T \vgamma, \sigma_1^2),  orall i \in [N], Y_{i, t} \sim 
ormal(	heta_i, \sigma_2^2),  orall i \in A_{t}, R_t = \sum_{i \in A_t} Y_{i,t}, where it is typically assumed that $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$ are known. We choose the prior $\vgamma \sim 
ormal(\vmu_{\vgamma}, {\Cov}_{\vgamma})$ with parameters as known.

algorithms.name: MTSS (Meta Thompson Sampling for Structured bandits)

symbols.Gamma: almost-sure upper bound on Gamma_t in the per-round decomposition E_t[Delta_t] <= Gamma_t sqrt(I_t(theta;A_t,Y_t)) + eps_t

conditions: the per-round decomposition E_t[Delta_t] <= Gamma_t sqrt(I_t(theta;A_t,Y_t)) + eps_t holds for all t

source.label: general regret bound
source.quote: Suppose that \eqref{eqn:Delta_decomp} holds for all $t$. Assume $\Gamma_t \le \Gamma$ almost surely for some $\Gamma$. Then for Algorithm \ref{alg:main_TS}, $BR(T)$ is bounded by \Gamma\sum_{t}\Mean[\sqrt{I_{t}(\vgamma;A_{t},\vY_{t})}] + \sum_{t}\Gamma\Mean[\sqrt{I_{t}(\vthe;A_{t},\vY_{t}|\vgamma)}] + \Mean[\epsilon_{t}].

results.notes: Abstract information-theoretic bound; expressed via declared symbols. First term: price of not knowing gamma; second: oracle-TS regret.

bound.expression: c_1*m*sqrt(T*d)*sqrt(log(1 + N_items*lambda_1/(sigma_1**2 + sigma_2**2/T))) + c_1*sqrt(N_items*T*m)*sqrt(log(1 + sigma_1**2*T/sigma_2)) + m*sqrt(2*(lambda_1 + sigma_1**2)/N_items)

symbols.N_items: number of items (base arms), paper's N
symbols.lambda_1: largest eigenvalue of the prior covariance Sigma_gamma
symbols.sigma_1: std of item parameter around x_i^T gamma (LMM)

conditions: data generated from the LMM hierarchical model (correctly specified)

source.label: Theorem1
source.quote: Under Assumptions 1-2, the Bayes regret of the MTSS under model (LMM) is bounded by c_1 K\sqrt{Td}\sqrt{ log(1+\frac{N\lambda_{1}(\Sigma_{\vgamma})}{\sigma_{1}^{2}+\sigma_{2}^{2}/T})} + c_1\sqrt{NTK}\sqrt{log(1 + \frac{\sigma_{1}^{2}}{\sigma_{2}}T)} + K\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}(\lambda_{1}(\Sigma_{\vgamma}) + \sigma_{1}^{2})} =\TO(K\sqrt{Td} + \sqrt{NTK}), where c_1 = 4\sqrt{...log(4NT^{2})}

results.notes: Paper's K (max slate size) mapped to m; paper's N (number of items) declared N_items; d is the feature dimension. Note sigma_2 (not sigma_2^2) appears in the second log as printed. c_1's definition uses 2log(...) in denominator in the theorem statement.

symbols.N_items: number of items (base arms), paper's N
